To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified 17 QQL for body composition and 7 for abdominal fatness, and several sex-antagonist and sex-specific QQL.
we have used Bayesian model selection in an F2 chicken population to comprehensively map the main, epistasic and sex-specific QQL for body composition.
We identified 17 QQL with main effects across thirteen chromosomes and several sex specific and sex-antogonistic QTL for somatic growth and body composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic architecture of body composition and abdominal adiposity in an F2 intercross between two divergently selected lines of chickens.
the identification of genetic loci and their interactions with sex that influence growth in chickens.
the identification of QTL for body weight, breast and thigh + drumstick muscle yields and abdominal fatness in a chicken F2 population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genetic architecture underlying body composition and abdominal adiposity is complex and involves many QTL, both main and epistatic, with some of these having sex-specific or sex-antagonism effects.
the genetic basis of somatic growth is complex and involves both main and interactive effects of genes, which may act differently in males and females.

QTL mapping for body composition in an F2 intercross between two extreme lines of chicken divergently selected on growth rate, identified 17 main effects QTL, several sex-specific and epistatic QTL, and that the genetic basis of somatic growth in chickens is complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
QTL controlling breast meat yield and abdominal fat are sex-specific.
the genetic basis of growth and body composition in chickens is complex and involves both main effects and interactions between genes.
the QTL for body fatness are different for the two sexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a reciprocal F2 design is a powerful approach for the detection of sex-dimorphic and sex-specific QQL.
sex-antagonism and sex-specific QQL play a major role in determining body composition traits in chicken.

QTL mapping in the F2 reciprocal inter-cross between the two lines is a powerful strategy for detecting QTL with main and epistatic effects, as well as for detecting sex-dimorphic and sex-antogonistic QTL.
